description:
Domain Terraforming Initiative
Terraforming as a megaproject: you build a Terraforming Control on a colony, then run long projects that change the world's conditions and, in the end, its planet type.

Release notes | Bugs and ideas (GitHub issues)

Requires: Starsector 0.98a, LunaLib
Optional: Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge), Console Commands
Works with Version Checker and TriOS.

This is a test version. 0.4.3 has every terraforming structure, but not the quests yet (they come in a later version). Without AoTD every structure is unlocked from the start, so for now you can try all of it in one game. Please tell me what breaks, what is too slow and what is too cheap, as that is exactly what this version is for.

What it adds

Terraforming here is not one building that fixes a planet. You put a Terraforming Control on the colony, then each structure works on one problem of the world (its air, its heat, its light and so on), and when the conditions change enough the planet changes its type. A project takes time and goods, so it is a long investment, not a quick fix.

The Terraforming Control and 24 terraforming structures. Each one works on one thing: a toxic, dense, thin or missing atmosphere, heat and cold, poor light and darkness, tectonic activity, extreme weather, pollution, an inimical biosphere, radiation. Others bring water with comets or take it away, improve the soil, seed marine life, or make a mild climate.
Reverse projects. The Atmospheric Siphon, the Deep Core Extractor and the Volatiles Extractor take resources from a world, at a price.
Colony Development. Civic Integration, Labor Camps and the Purge Detachment work on the colony's people. Domed Cities (Sky Cities on a gas giant, Seafloor Cities on a water world), the City Agrav Grid and the Impact Defense Grid protect a colony from its hazards. Hydroponic Farms feed a colony that has no farmland.
24 special items that make projects faster or cheaper. They wear out, so they are not a one-time install.
Projects take goods. A short supply stops a project, and a long one makes it lose progress.
DTI Projects in the Intel screen (Terraforming tag), with every running project by colony, so you do not have to open each colony to check.
Settings in LunaLib. You can switch terraforming or Colony Development off, turn single kinds of projects off, and change the numbers.

Surasheel, a Barren World, with the Terraforming Control, an Atmospheric Forge at work and Domed Cities.

The same planet three times: Barren, then Barren-Desert, then Jungle.

DTI Projects: every project by colony, its progress and the goods it is short of. On the left, the history entry of each planet.

More screenshots

The Atmospheric Forge after a long shortage: 5 kinds of goods are short, so it loses progress. The tooltip also shows the planet type the project leads to.

With AoTD: the DTI research tab.

Structures and items
Every structure with its picture and its description from the game, by group.

The Terraforming Control

Atmosphere

Temperature

Light

Tectonics, weather, pollution, biosphere, radiation

Water

Soil and farmland

Marine life

Climate

Reverse projects

Colony Development

Items
All 24 items in one picture: 12 kinds, each one pristine and worn.

How to unlock the structures

The quests are not in the mod yet, so there are two ways for now:

With AoTD: research the techs on the DTI tab (28 techs, on their own tab).
Without AoTD: every structure is unlocked from the start. The LunaLib setting Unlock without quests (DTI, General tab) does this, and it stays on by default until the quests are in the mod.

Install and saves

Unzip the folder into Starsector/mods and enable "Domain Terraforming Initiative" in the launcher (or in TriOS).
Adding to a running game: you can. A running game misses only the marine life that a new sector places on some water worlds, and a Reef Seeder can still bring marine life to a water world.
Removing from a save: you cannot. Once you save a game with DTI on, that save needs DTI to load, even if you never built or researched anything from it. Keep a copy of your save from before you add DTI.

Compatibility

I tested it with Nexerelin, AoTD, DIY Planets and TaSC. With AoTD the structures come with research on their own tab, and the AoTD workshop can make the DTI items. Also, with Console Commands you get five test commands: DTI_Unlock, DTI_Status, DTI_Progress, DTI_Short and DTI_Sun.

Bugs and ideas

All work on the mod happens on GitHub. Please report bugs and ideas in the issues (for a crash, add your mod list and starsector.log), and pull requests are welcome, the Java source is in src/. An issue is easier for me to track than a forum reply, as nothing gets lost between pages.

Changelog
0.4.3
Comet Shepherd on Barren-Desert: a Barren-Desert with no hard condition (very cold, very hot, no, thin or toxic atmosphere, irradiated, darkness) was stuck: no structure could change its type. The Comet Shepherd now works there and makes it Arid.

0.4.2
A calm Captive Sun: a small yellow star in orbit, in place of the pulsing lamp. It still lights the planet's night side. A Captive Sun you built before turns into the star when you load the game.
Planet history: in the Terraforming tab of the Intel screen, each planet with a Terraforming Control gets an entry with DTI's events and their dates. It stays when you lose the colony, and you can delete it.
A console command for tests: dti_sun.

0.4.1
Unlock without quests is on by default: without AoTD, every structure is unlocked from the start. With AoTD, the research still unlocks them. The setting goes back to off when the quests are in the mod. A game that already saved this setting in LunaLib keeps its value.

0.4.0, the first public test version
The Terraforming Control and 24 terraforming structures, with planet type changes.
The reverse projects: Atmospheric Siphon, Deep Core Extractor, Volatiles Extractor.
Colony Development: Civic Integration, Labor Camps, Purge Detachment, Domed Cities, the City Agrav Grid, the Impact Defense Grid, Hydroponic Farms.
24 special items.
DTI Projects in the Intel screen.
With AoTD: 28 techs on their own research tab.
LunaLib settings.

What comes next
This is the plan by version, with no dates. It can change, and the order can change too, mostly from what you report. If you have an idea, open an issue on GitHub (the link is above).
0.4.5: achievements (with MagicLib, which stays optional), the old and the new planet in the history when a world changes its type, small ecology events with a choice during long projects, and Eridani-Utopia contracts to terraform other factions' worlds.
0.5: the DTI Planner in the Intel screen: pick a colony and a goal, and it queues the structures for you. It also shows what a planet you surveyed can become.
0.5.5: a terraforming black market, a shop for DTI items.
0.6: the hypershunt line, the planet creation line, and stations.
0.7: the quests: the unlock paths and some hidden content.
0.8: AI factions terraform their own worlds.
0.9: AI raids on your research, and a smarter AI.
1.0: the full release, after the last tests and bug fixes.

Credits and permissions
Thanks to Alex and the Fractal Softworks team for building Starsector, a great game with the room for mods like this one.

Inspired by DIY Planets (kentington, now the community edition) and Terraforming & Station Construction (boggled). DTI takes ideas only: it has no code, text or art from them, and all the art was made for this mod.

License: MIT, for the code, data, text and art. See LICENSE.

AI use disclaimer
This mod was made with AI tools:
Art (building pictures, item icons, tech icons, and condition icons): Gemini Flash in the Gemini web app, Gemini 3.5 Flash.
Texts: Claude Opus 5.5, as a text helper that helped proofread and fix issues in the texts.
Code: Claude Opus 5.5, as a code helper that helped write most of the code and configs.

No extra training data was used.

The mod includes 24 specialized structures for various environmental problems, reverse extraction projects, and colony development options like domed cities and hydroponic farms. Projects consume resources and time, with progress tracked in an Intel screen interface.
